titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§230–236: The Night Guard's Charge
about: Chinggis Qahan praises his night guard for keeping him safe through storms and enemies, names the elder guards and the great day guards and quiver-bearers, and entrusts his ten thousand guardsmen to his heirs (§§230–231). §232 gives the night guard charge of the palace tents and carts, the standard and drum, the vessels, the food and drink, the door and the camp, and §233 holds the guard back from war unless the Qahan himself takes the field. §234 sets out where the guard, the quiver-bearers and the day guards stand in camp. §235 is the submission of Arslan Qan of the Qarluq to Qubilai, and §236 Sübegetei's pursuit of Toqto'a's sons to the river Chu. Grammar to watch: the third-person optative in -tuγai/-tügei, the converb chains in -žu/-žü, the possessive -tei/-ten, and the plural imperative of keġe-. Shiratori's quotation marks are only partly printed, and the notes say where one is supplied.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan, saying:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün is the usual frame for the Qahan's own words: ügülerün is ügüle- 'to speak' with the converb of time -rün (Ming 說), 'when saying'. Shiratori's colon follows, and his opening quotation mark stands on the next word. The speech praises the night guard, who kept watch over the Qahan's sleep, and runs to the closing mark on the last keġedkün of the section. The speech is long, so I have cut it into short units.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Eġületei süni örügetei ger min-u eġeren kebtežü örüg nuta untaγ̇ulžu
sentences.l: "Cloud-having night, skylight-having house my, around lying, peace quiet having-made-sleep,
sentences.i: “On cloudy nights, lying all round my tent with its skylight, they let me sleep in peace and quiet,
sentences.n: Read the endings first. -tei is the possessive 'having' (Ming 有的): eġületei 'cloud-having', örügetei 'skylight-having'. The chain is a converb chain: kebtežü 'lying' (-žü, Ming 着) and untaγ̇ulžu 'having made sleep', the causative -γ̇ul- 'make, let' plus -žu. The subject, 'my night guard', only arrives in the next unit. Doubtful: eġületei süni örügetei ger could also be read 'on the cloudy night, in the tent with a skylight'; örüge 'skylight' rests on the Ming 天窓 alone, and eġeren 'surrounding' (Ming 圍) is taken as eġere- plus the converb -n. The glossary has eġere- 'to attack' (Ming 攻, in eġerekün); 'to besiege, encircle' would join that with the Ming 圍 here, but this is a guess.

sentences.t: ene oron-dur kürgegsen ötöküs kebteġül min-u
sentences.l: This place-in brought-who elders night-guard my,
sentences.i: my elders of the night guard, who brought me to this place,
sentences.n: kürgegsen is the past participle (-gsen, Ming 的) of kürge- 'to bring to': 'the ones who brought'. The phrase is the first of two statements of the same kindness: they brought me here (a place of rank), and, at the end of the next stretch, to a high place.

sentences.t: hodutai süni ordo ger min-u horčin kebtežü oron dotora ese oγžadγaγsan ölžeten
sentences.l: Star-having night, palace house my around lying, bed within not startled-ones, fortune-having-ones,
sentences.i: on starry nights, lying round my palace tent, who never startled me in my bed — the fortunate ones —
sentences.n: Again -tei 'having' (hodutai, Ming 星有的 'star-having night'). ese is the negative of a past act, as against ülü for the present, and it stands before oγžadγaγsan, a participle: oγžad- 'be startled' (the glossary's oγžadču) with the causative -γa- (Ming 敎 'cause') and -γsan, 'the ones who did not frighten (me)'. oron dotora is 'inside the bed' (Ming 被窠 'quilt'; oron elsewhere is 'place, seat'). ölžeten, the last word of this unit, goes with the kebteġül that opens the next ('fortunate night guard', as in the naming order below): the cut falls between the adjective and its noun, so `i` sets 'the fortunate ones' between dashes. hodutai is hodun 'star' (the glossary's word, Ming 星) with its -n dropped before -tai. Doubtful: the sense of oγžad- rests on the Ming 驚 alone.

sentences.t: kebteġül min-u ündür oron-dur kürgebe.
sentences.l: Night-guard my, high place-in brought.
sentences.i: my night guard brought me to a high seat.
sentences.n: The finite verb at last: kürgebe, kürge- 'bring to' with the past -be (Ming 了). ölžeten, the last word of the unit before, is ölže 'good fortune, blessing' (the glossary's word; Ming 吉慶, 'auspicious') with the possessive -ten, 'fortune-having, fortunate', and qualifies the kebteġül that begins this unit. oron-dur ündür: 'at the high place', which I render 'seat' because the Qahan means his rank. Shiratori's full stop closes the sentence; the whole of it, from Eġületei, is one long sentence, and I broke it where each participle ends.

sentences.t: Šilžirin büküi boroγ̇on-a silgüdgen büküi žüġen-e čidγun büküi qura-da
sentences.l: Moving being, to-the-blizzard; making-tremble being, to-the-cold; pouring being, to-the-rain,
sentences.i: through the drifting blizzard, the shaking cold, the pouring rain,
sentences.n: The model of the line is a participle in -küi, büküi, 'being' (bü- 'to be', Ming 有的), after a participle or noun, three times over, each followed by a dative-locative that the Ming marks 行 (-a, -e, -da: to, in the face of). So 'being in motion, to the blizzard'. The three weather words are boroγ̇an 'blizzard' (Ming 風雪 'wind and snow'), žüġen 'cold', qura 'rain'. Doubtful: silgüdgen (Ming 敎顫 'make shiver') and čidγun (Ming 傾下的 'poured down') are single morphs I could not analyse, and šilžirin's ending is guessed.

sentences.t: Iburun büküi daisun dotora irgetei ger min-u horčin hirmes ülü kin idγažu baiγsad itegelten kebteġül min-u
sentences.l: Turmoil being, enemies among, irge-having house my around, blink not doing, withstanding, having-stood, reliance-having night-guard my,
sentences.i: among enemies in turmoil, standing round my tent without a blink and holding firm, my trusty night guard,
sentences.n: A long chain, kept whole because it is one noun phrase: two participles (büküi and baiγsad 'those who stood') and a possessive noun (itegelten, itegel 'reliance' + -ten, 'trust-having, reliable') hang on kebteġül min-u, 'my night guard'. idγažu (Ming 當着) is idqa- 'to restrain', stem uncertain; hirmes ülü kin 'a blink, not doing' (Ming 瞬眼). iburun büküi daisun is read as in the weather line (šilžirin büküi boroγ̇on-a): büküi makes the word before it an attribute of the noun after it, so 'enemies in turmoil' (Ming 紛攘, 'confusion'; one morph, its ending unclear). Doubtful: irgetei (Ming 地𢫯 有的) has a rare character in the Ming; the glossary's irge ('people', Ming 百姓, or 'wether') does not match it, so the stem is left unrendered and `i` says only 'my tent'.

sentences.t: ölžeten kebteġül min-u ötöküs kebteġül keġegdün.
sentences.l: Fortunate night-guard my, elders night-guard: say-(you)!
sentences.i: Call them my fortunate night guard, the elder night guard.
sentences.n: The first of four naming orders, all ending in a plural imperative (Ming 說您, 'you (all) say'): keġegdün and below keġedkün, which I take to be the polite plural command in -dqun's family (compare -dqun in 227–229). So 'call (them) …'. Unlike the three orders that follow, no accusative marks a group here, so I take the group to be the guard just described and both phrases to be its names; one phrase as the group and the other as its new name cannot be excluded. This keġegdün (Ming 說您) is not the passive keġegdekün (Ming 被說每) of earlier parts. keġe- is 'to say'.

sentences.t: Ögöle čerbi-lüġe oroγsad dalan turγag-i jekes turγaγ̇ud keġegdün.
sentences.l: Ögöle with-cherbi entered-ones seventy day-guards (acc.), great day-guards: say-(you)!
sentences.i: The seventy day guards who joined Ögöle the cherbi: call them the great day guards.
sentences.n: turγag-i is the day guard, turγaγ (a house rendering; the Ming 散班 means 'scattered shift'), with the accusative -i; jekes is jeke 'great' with the plural -s (Ming 大每), the new name; keġegdün is the order, 'call (them)'. čerbi-lüġe: čerbi (an office whose meaning is unknown) + the comitative -lüġe 'together with'. oroγsad (Ming 入的每) 'those who have entered' means joined. The case ending stands on the last word of the phrase, as in Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur, so Ögöle čerbi-lüġe is 'with Ögöle the cherbi'.

sentences.t: Jesün-Teġe, Bugidai-tan qorčin-i jekes qorčin keġedkün"
sentences.l: Jesün-Teġe, Bugidai and-the-like quiver-bearers (acc.), great quiver-bearers: say-(you)!"
sentences.i: Jesün-Te'e, Bügidei and the other quiver-bearers: call them the great quiver-bearers.”
sentences.n: -tan on Bugidai-tan is the possessive plural 'having', which the Ming reads 等, 'and so on'. The Han here (不吉歹) is that of Bügidei in §225; §234 prints Bukidai (不乞歹), which I take to be the same man beside the same Jesün-Te'e. I follow the house name Bügidei in `i` and in the lemma, and the print in `l`. Shiratori's closing quotation mark stands on keġedkün, closing the speech opened at Eġületei.

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Saying, decree became.
sentences.i: So he said, issuing a decree.
sentences.n: keġen žarliγ bolba, the end of the decree frame: keġe- 'say', converb -n, then žarliγ bol- 'to become a decree', that is, 'to issue a decree' (Ming 聖旨 做了).

sentences.t: "Jeren tabun miṅγad-ača min-u beje čaγ̇ada emčülen ilγažu iregsed tümen emčü kešigten-i min-u
sentences.l: "Ninety-five from-thousands, my body at-side, privately picking-out, those-who-came ten-thousand private guardsmen (acc.) my,
sentences.i: “My ten thousand personal guardsmen, who came specially picked out from the ninety-five thousands to be at my side,
sentences.n: jeren tabun miṅγad-ača, 'ninety five' + 'thousand' in the plural with the ablative -ača, is 95 thousands, that is, the thousand-households, here 'from the ninety-five thousands'. čaγ̇ada (Ming 貼身) is 'at my side'; ilγažu 'picking out', iregsed 'those who came'. emčü and emčülen (Ming 梯已) 'private, one's own': I read the second as an adverbial form, uncertain. The Ming glosses stand 貼 under beje and 身 under čaγ̇ada; together they are 貼身 'close to the person', as elsewhere, so the two seem transposed. kešigten-i is the guardsman with accusative -i: the object of the verb that arrives in the third unit (asaradqun). The first long clause, in other words, is a set of attributes; I break it from the next at the end of the object.

sentences.t: Ede tümen kešigten-i min-u nendüġüd qutuγ keġežü ülü-ü aduγ̇ai" keġebe.
sentences.l: These ten-thousand guardsmen (acc.) my, good-fortunes blessing saying: not-? let-it-be" he-said.
sentences.i: These ten thousand guardsmen of mine, calling them my good fortunes and my blessing: should it not be so?” he said.
sentences.n: The ending is the hardest part of the section and I give it as a conjecture. nendüġüd qutuγ keġežü is 'calling (them) nendüġüd qutuγ', on the pattern of the naming orders above (keġe- 'to call'): nendüġüd is nendü 'good fortune' (the glossary's word, as in §207) with a plural ending, Ming 福(每), and qutuγ (Ming 神, 'spirit', elsewhere 'fortune, blessing'). Then ülü-ü aduγ̇ai, which the Ming glosses 不 有者麽: ülü is 'not', -ü may be a question particle (the Ming puts its 麽 on the next word), and aduγ̇ai may be a- 'be' with an optative (-duγ̇ai for -tuγai). So 'should it not be so?', a rhetorical question, probable but not secure; a negative wish, 'let it not be otherwise', is the other possibility. The closing quotation mark stands on aduγ̇ai.

sentences.t: "Ordo-jin čerbin ökid-i ger-ün köġüd temeġečin-i hükečin-i kebteġül basaγ̇alažu ordo-jin ger tergen-i asaratuγai.
sentences.l: "Of-palace cherbi, girls (acc.), of-house sons, camel-herders (acc.), cattle-herders (acc.), night-guard taking-account, of-palace tents, carts (acc.) let-them-gather-up.
sentences.i: “Let the night guard, taking account of the palace's cherbi, its girls, the sons of its households, its camel-herders and cattle-herders, look after the palace's tents and carts.
sentences.n: The first of a run of third-person orders in -tuγai (the optative of the third person: 'let …', the Ming 者). The accusatives -i (Ming 行) mark the objects, a list of palace people: čerbin (čerbi + -n, plural or stem-n, Ming 官名), ökid-i 'girls', köġüd 'sons', temeġečin-i, hükečin-i. basaγ̇alažu (Ming 知料, 'reckon') and asaratuγai (Ming 收拾, 'put in order') give the two verbs; both stems are inferred from the Ming. Doubtful: whether the whole list is the object of basaγ̇ala- or of the second verb too. The opening quotation mark is Shiratori's.

sentences.i: “If food and drink are wasted, let us seek it from the night guard who had charge of them,” he said.

What is sought (the loss, the culprit) is not said.

Doubtful: the sense 'without counsel from the night guard' (the ablative -eče is odd here).

sentences.i: When food is given out, let it be given out first, beginning with the night guard,” he said.
sentences.n: teriġülen (Ming 爲頭, 'take as head') is teriġüle- with the converb -n, 'beginning with'; urida 'first, beforehand'; the verb is again tügeġe- 'give out', here with the optative -tügei. Shiratori's closing quotation mark stands on tügeġetügei.

sentences.t: "Ordo ger-tür oroqu γarqu-ji kebteġül žasatuγai.
sentences.l: "Palace tent-to entering going-out-(acc.) night-guard let-regulate.
sentences.i: “Let the night guard regulate those who enter and those who leave the palace tent.
sentences.n: oroqu γarqu-ji: two participles in -qu (Ming 的), 'the entering', 'the going out', the second carrying the accusative -ji (the form after a vowel, the Ming 行). ger-tür is the dative-locative 'to the tent'. žasatuγai: žasa- 'put in order' + the optative. The opening quotation mark is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: Egüden-dür kebteġül-ün eġüdečin ger čaγ̇ada baituγai.
sentences.l: Door-at night-guard's door-keepers tent side-at let-stand.
sentences.i: At the door, let the night guard's door-keepers stand close by the tent.
sentences.n: egüden-dür is egüden 'door' (the Ming's 門 'gate') + the dative-locative -dür (Ming 裏 'in'). eġüdečin (Ming 把門的) is the door-keeper, egüden + the agent -či + -n. čaγ̇ada 'at the side', baituγai from bai- 'stand'.

sentences.t: Kebteġül-eče qojar orožu jeke tüsürge barin atuγai" keġebe.
sentences.l: Night-guard-from two entering big banquet holding let-be," said.
sentences.i: Let two of the night guard go in and stay to hold the great banquet,” he said.
sentences.n: qojar 'two' follows the Ming 兩箇 'two'; orožu is oro- 'enter' with -žu; barin is bari- 'to hold' + the converb -n; atuγai from a- 'to be' + the optative, 'let them stay'. tüsürge (Ming 酒局, 'wine office') is the 'banquet, drinking-party' of the glossary's tüsürge-jin, and the glossary's earlier 'jar' (Ming 甕) is another sense of the spelling; 'to hold the great banquet' (barin, bari- 'hold') is uncertain. Shiratori's closing mark is on atuγai.

morph.gloss: banquet, drinking-party (as in the glossary's tüsürge-jin; Ming 酒局 'wine office'; uncertain) [酒局]
optative, third person: let it be

sentences.t: "Kebteġül-eče nutuγ̇učiṅ jabužu ordo ger baγ̇ultuγai" keġebe.
sentences.l: "Night-guard-from camp-managers going, palace tent let-make-alight," said.
sentences.i: “Let the camp-managers from the night guard go and pitch the palace tents,” he said.
sentences.n: nutuγ̇učiṅ is the camp-manager (nutuγ 'camping-ground' + an agent ending, the Ming 管營盤的 'those in charge of the camp'), the ending uncertain. baγ̇ultuγai is baγ̇u- 'to alight' + the causative -l- + -tuγai, 'let them have it alight', that is, pitch it. 'Go and' renders jabužu 'going'.

morph.gloss: agent ending (uncertain): the one in charge of …
causative: make … (for -γ̇ul-, the γ̇u absorbed after baγ̇u-, as in baγ̇uludqun)

sentences.t: Bidan-i šibaγ̇ulaqui abalaqui-dur kebteġül bidan-luγ̇a šibaγ̇ulaldun abalaldun jabutuγai.

sentences.i: “When we go hawking and hunting, let the night guard go with us, hawking and hunting together.
sentences.n: Shiratori prints no opening mark on this speech, only the closing one on talbituγai; I supply it in `i`. šibaγ̇ulaqui abalaqui-dur: two participles, the second with the dative-locative -dur, 'when hawking, when hunting' (šibaγ̇ula- 'hawk' has an uncertain stem). šibaγ̇ulaldun and abalaldun carry -ldu-, 'together, jointly' (Ming 共), plus the converb -n; jabutuγai 'let them go'. bidan-luγ̇a is 'with us', the comitative -luγ̇a.

sentences.l: Carts-in some-of-own judging let-put," said.
sentences.i: Let them load some of their own in the carts, judging the amount,” he said.
sentences.n: žarimud(i)-jan is žarim 'part' (Ming 一伴) with the plural -ud and the reflexive-possessive -(i)jan 'one's own'; what is loaded, the thing itself, is not named. čaγlažu 'judging' (Ming 斟酌), talbituγai 'let them put' (talbi-). Doubtful: žarim, and so 'some of their own'.

sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, saying:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: The same frame as §232, ügülerün 'when saying'. The speech that follows has several parts; the first is a rule that the guard goes to war only with the Qahan.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Bidan-u beje čerig ese γaruγ̇asu
sentences.l: "Our body army not goes-out if,
sentences.i: “If our own army does not take the field,
sentences.n: ese γaruγ̇asu: ese 'not' (Ming 不) before γar- 'go out' with the conditional -uγ̇asu (Ming 呵), 'if (it) does not go out'. bidan-u beje čerig (Ming 咱的身軍) is 'our body-army', which I take as our personal army, the one led by ourselves; this is doubtful, and I read it so because the next clause sets the guard against it.

sentences.t: kebteġül bidan-ača aṅgida čerig bu γartuγai" keġebe.
sentences.l: Night-guard us-from apart army not let-go-out," said.
sentences.i: let no army of the night guard go out apart from us,” he said.
sentences.n: bidan-ača is 'from us' (ablative -ača), aṅgida 'apart, besides' (Ming 外); bu with the optative γartuγai is the prohibition (Ming 休 … 者). kebteġül may also be the subject, 'let the night guard not go out to war apart from us'; where 'the night guard's army' is meant, as below, Shiratori's text has the genitive (kebteġül-ün čerig). The sense that the guard may not campaign without the Qahan follows the Ming and the previous clause.

sentences.t: "Ein keġeġülüġed žarliγ dabažu kebteġül-i naitažu
sentences.l: "Thus having-had-said, decree transgressing, night-guard (acc.) envying,
sentences.i: “This having been said, whoever transgresses the decree and, envying the night guard,
sentences.n: A converb chain, broken in two: keġeġülüġed, keġe- 'say' + the causative -ġül- + -ġed, Ming 被說了, 'having had it said'; dabažu 'crossing over' (Ming 越着), which is 'transgressing'; naitažu 'envying' (naita-, stem inferred from the Ming 嫉妒), with kebteġül-i, the night guard, as its object. The subject is in the next unit.

morph.gloss: to envy (stem inferred from the Ming 嫉妒) [嫉妬着]

sentences.t: čerig γarγaqun čerig medekü čerbin aldaltan boltuγai" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Army those-who-send-out, army managing cherbi, penalty-having let-be," saying decree became.
sentences.i: sends out an army — the cherbi who command armies — shall be liable to punishment,” so saying, he issued a decree.

Shiratori's closing mark is on boltuγai.

sentences.t: "Kebteġül-ün čerig ker ülü γarγaγdamui keġemüi-že ta.
sentences.l: "Night-guard's army how not is-made-to-go-out say-indeed you.
sentences.i: “You say, ‘How is it that the night guard's army is not sent out?’
sentences.n: Shiratori's opening mark stands on Kebteġül-ün, so the Qahan's argument begins here. keġemüi-že is keġe- 'say', the present -müi, and -že 'indeed'; ta is 'you' (polite plural). ker ülü γarγaγdamui is 'how is it not made to go out?' with the causative -γa- and the passive -γda- (Ming 被出有). The inner quotation marks are mine; Shiratori prints none.

sentences.t: Kebteġül- lü min-u altan amin sakimui.
sentences.l: Night-guard only my golden life guards.
sentences.i: Only the night guard watch over my golden life.
sentences.n: The word kebteġül- is cut by a line break; the next word, lü, carries on from it (the hyphen is the printer's). lü is a particle that the Ming glosses 但 'only, but'; the glossary has the same -lu in bidan-lu (Ming 咱但), and the sense is uncertain. altan amin is 'golden life', the Ming 金性命, so 'precious life'. sakimui: saki- 'to guard' + the present tense -mui (Ming 有).

sentences.i: When we go hawking and hunting, they share the toil.

sentences.t: Ordo qadaγalaγ̇uldažu neġüküi-dür örüg-tür terge asaramui.
sentences.l: Palace having-been-made-to-guard moving-when, quiet-at, cart gather-up.
sentences.i: Given charge of the palace, when we break camp and when we are at rest, they tend the carts.
sentences.n: neġüküi-dür is 'when moving camp' (neġü-, Ming 起); örüg-tür is örüg 'peace' + the dative-locative, 'at peace', Ming 寗靜時. qadaγalaγ̇uldažu (Ming 被敎管着, 'caused to be managed') has a causative -γ̇ul- and what I take as a passive -da-; the sense, 'put in charge of the palace', is secure but the analysis is not.

sentences.t: Min-u beje sakižu qonoqu kilbar-u bi.
sentences.l: My body guarding lodging easy-? is.
sentences.i: Is it easy to pass the night guarding my person?
sentences.n: kilbar-u bi (Ming 容易麽有) is 'is (it) easy?': kilbar 'easy' with the question -u, then bi 'is'. sakižu 'guarding' and qonoqu (Ming 宿, 'to lodge'), a participle in -qu; the stem qono- is inferred. A rhetorical question.

sentences.t: Ger tergen jeke aγ̇uruγ neġüküi-dür saγ̇uqui-dur asaraqui kilbar-u bi.
sentences.l: Tents carts great rear-camp moving-when settling-when gather-up easy-? is.
sentences.i: Is it easy, when we move and when we settle, to see to the tents, the carts and the great rear camp?
sentences.n: A second rhetorical question in the same pattern as the last. aγ̇uruγ (Ming 老營 here, 老小營 'camp of the old and the young' in earlier parts) is the rear camp, where the old, the children and the baggage stayed. neġüküi-dür, saγ̇uqui-dur 'when moving, when settling' (participle + dative-locative); asaraqui is the participle of asara- 'tend', here nominal.

to gather up, look after (stem inferred from the Ming 收拾) [收拾的]

sentences.t: Tein dabqur qaγas qaγas jabudaltan keġežü
sentences.l: Thus double separating separating going-ones saying,
sentences.i: ‘Thus, doubled and separated, those who go about’, saying,
sentences.n: I do not understand this clause and have kept it literal. tein 'thus', dabqur 'double, layered' (Ming 重), qaγas qaγas 'separating, separating' (Ming 分離 twice), jabudaltan 'those who go about'; keġežü 'saying'. Possibly it means 'going off in separate bands again and again'. The inner quotation marks are mine.

morph.gloss: to go, move about [行動 有的每]

sentences.t: bidan-ača aṅgida öġere čerig bu jabutuγai keġeküi teimü bi-že" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Us-from apart other army not let-go, saying so it-is indeed," he-said.
sentences.i: ‘Let no other army go apart from us’ — so it is said indeed,” he said.
sentences.n: bidan-ača aṅgida: 'apart from us' again; öġere čerig, 'another army' (öġere, Ming 別); bu … jabutuγai the prohibition. keġeküi teimü bi-že: the participle 'the saying', teimü 'so', bi-že 'is indeed'. Shiratori's closing mark is on bi-že; the verb keġežüġüi is a past in -žüġüi.

sentences.t: Basa žarliγ bolurun:
sentences.l: Again decree becoming-when:
sentences.i: Again, when he issued a decree:
sentences.n: bolurun is bol- 'become' with -urun, the converb of time (Ming 做); žarliγ bolurun is the stock phrase, here 'when he decreed'. The colon opens a run of orders, most of them in -tuγai.

sentences.t: "Šigi-Qutuqu-luγ̇a žarγu kebteġül-eče žarγu sonosulčatuγai" keġebe.
sentences.l: "Šigi-Qutuqu-with judgement, night-guard-from judgement let-hear-together," said.
sentences.i: “Let judges from the night guard hear cases together with Shigi-Qutuqu,” he said.
sentences.n: -luγ̇a is the comitative 'with' (Ming 一同). žarγu (Ming 斷事) 'judgement, the judge's office' stands twice; I read the first as the cases heard and the second, with kebteġül-eče, as the judges from the night guard. sonosulčatuγai: sonos- 'to hear' + a 'together' element (Ming 共) + the optative. Doubtful: the doubled žarγu, and whether the night guard are the judges or the ones judged.

morph.gloss: man's name, Shigi-Qutuqu [人名 一同]
judgement, lawsuit, the judge's office [斷事]

sentences.t: "Kebteġül-eče qor numu qujaγ žebe asaražu tügeġeldütügei.
sentences.l: "Night-guard-from quivers, bows, armour, gear gathering let-be-shared-together.
sentences.i: “From the night guard, let quivers, bows, armour and weapons be gathered and shared out.
sentences.n: žebe here is the common noun 'weapon, gear' (Ming 器械); the same letters are the name Jebe elsewhere. tügeġeldütügei: tügeġe- 'give out' + -ldü- 'together' (Ming 共 敎) + -tügei. asaražu 'gathering' is the converb. The Ming 宿衞處 for -eče is 'at the night guard's place', which allows 'from their stock' or 'from their men'. The Ming 敎 ('cause') before 共 is not accounted for; it may mark 'have it shared out together'.

sentences.t: Aγtas-ača asaražu oγ̇ošin ačižu jabutuγai" keġebe.

sentences.t: Qubilai nojan-i Qarluγ̇ud-tur čaγ̇uraγ̇ulba.
sentences.l: Qubilai noyan (acc.) Qarluqs-against sent-out-on-campaign.
sentences.i: He sent Qubilai the noyan against the Qarluq.
sentences.n: No subject is printed; the one who sends is the Qahan. čaγ̇uraγ̇ulba: čaγ̇ura- 'to go out on campaign' (inferred from the Ming 出征) with the causative -γ̇ul- and the past -ba, 'made go out'. sentences.n: ese bulγaba, 'not fought': bulγa- 'to fight' (Ming 厮殺 'fight hand to hand'), ese before a past form. The speaker is not named. The converbs keġen and sojurγažu share their subject with the closing verb bolba, whose subject is the Qahan, so I take the Qahan to say it, reasoning from Arslan's not fighting; but Shiratori's order (the quotation, then Čiṅgis Qaγan) would also allow Qubilai to say it as he presents Arslan. sojurγažu is sojurγa- 'show favour', the same word that opens decrees of reward elsewhere in this chronicle.

sentences.n: temür teregetü is 'iron cart-having' (Ming 銕車有的): an epithet: terege 'cart' (as in §199, teregetü-ji) with the possessive -tü. Merkid-ün Toγtoγ̇a-jin: Merkid with the genitive -ün, Toqto'a with -jin. teriġüten (Ming 等項 'and so on') is teriġü 'head' with the possessive -ten, 'the headed ones'; the Ming reads it 'and the rest'. in-ü is the third-person genitive after its noun: 'his', that is, Toqto'a's sons; it repeats Toqto'a and `i` does not. The unit has no verb; it hangs on the chain of the next.

The chain is short enough to keep in one unit.
